FICTIONAL PATIENT FOR SOFTWARE TESTING ONLY

Patient: Synthetic Elias Mercer
Age and sex: 46-year-old man
Clinic record number: SYN-EM-1017
Date of service: 17 October 2026
Treating clinician: Dr. Leena Farrow
Visit: Established-patient, in-person gastrointestinal outpatient visit.

S - Subjective
Synthetic Elias Mercer's chief concern is watery diarrhea lasting 11 days. He reports three to five loose or watery stools daily, with intermittent mild periumbilical cramping that improves after a bowel movement. He is eating and drinking and can keep fluids down. He denies blood in the stool, black stools, fever, vomiting, nighttime awakening to pass stool and unintentional weight loss.
He previously saw this same clinician, Dr. Leena Farrow, in this same GI clinic on 21 August 2026 for intermittent constipation. At that visit she recommended a four-week trial of psyllium and increased dietary fiber. His constipation resolved, and he completed the psyllium trial in September. He is no longer taking psyllium.
His relevant medical history is intermittent heartburn. He has no known history of inflammatory bowel disease or celiac disease and no prior abdominal surgery. His current medication is famotidine 20 mg by mouth as needed for heartburn. He reports an allergy to amoxicillin, which causes hives.

O - Objective
Blood pressure is 118/74 mmHg, pulse 76 beats per minute, temperature 36.8 degrees Celsius and weight 78 kg. He appears comfortable and well hydrated. His abdomen is soft, with mild periumbilical tenderness, normal bowel sounds and no guarding or rebound.

A - Assessment
Diarrhea and periumbilical abdominal pain were both evaluated during this encounter. The cause remains uncertain. Infectious and inflammatory causes remain possibilities; neither has been established. No definitive underlying disease is diagnosed at this encounter.

P - Plan
A stool bacterial pathogen PCR panel and fecal calprotectin are ordered today for sample collection after this visit. No stool sample was collected today, neither test was performed today and no results are available. No procedure was performed during this encounter.
The plan is oral hydration and food as tolerated while awaiting the stool studies. No new prescription medication is started. Follow-up is planned in two weeks, with earlier contact when results become available. He is advised to seek prompt assessment for bloody or black stools, fever, worsening abdominal pain or inability to maintain hydration.

Office E/M selection is based on total physician time on the date of service. Dr. Farrow personally spent 37 minutes on the encounter date: six minutes reviewing prior records, 24 minutes obtaining the history, performing the examination and counseling the patient, and seven minutes entering orders and documenting the visit. The 37 minutes exclude nine minutes of nursing rooming work and five minutes of physician record review performed on the preceding day. The total also excludes any time for separately reported services.

chapter:18.description: Symptoms, signs and abnormal clinical and laboratory findings, not elsewhere classified (R00-R99)

instructions.text: This chapter includes symptoms, signs, abnormal results of clinical or other investigative procedures, and ill-defined conditions regarding which no diagnosis classifiable elsewhere is recorded.

Signs and symptoms that point rather definitely to a given diagnosis have been assigned to a category in other chapters of the classification. In general, categories in this chapter include the less well-defined conditions and symptoms that, without the necessary study of the case to establish a final diagnosis, point perhaps equally to two or more diseases or to two or more systems of the body. Practically all categories in the chapter could be designated 'not otherwise specified', 'unknown etiology' or 'transient'. The Alphabetical Index should be consulted to determine which symptoms and signs are to be allocated here and which to other chapters. The residual subcategories, numbered .8, are generally provided for other relevant symptoms that cannot be allocated elsewhere in the classification.
The conditions and signs or symptoms included in categories R00-R94 consist of:
(a) cases for which no more specific diagnosis can be made even after all the facts bearing on the case have been investigated;
(b) signs or symptoms existing at the time of initial encounter that proved to be transient and whose causes could not be determined;
(c) provisional diagnosis in a patient who failed to return for further investigation or care;
(d) cases referred elsewhere for investigation or treatment before the diagnosis was made;
(e) cases in which a more precise diagnosis was not available for any other reason;
(f) certain symptoms, for which supplementary information is provided, that represent important problems in medical care in their own right.
